problemStatement:
A factory ventilation system uses an electric motor to drive a centrifugal blower through a V-belt and pulley arrangement. The belt carries unequal tensile forces on its tight and slack sides so that their difference produces the torque required at the motor pulley.

All numerical operating conditions, dimensions, equivalent belt area, and allowable stress are instructor-assigned representative teaching values and are not specifications extracted from the photograph.
engineeringGoal: Determine the tight-side and slack-side V-belt tensions required to transmit the specified motor power. Then, as an instructor-defined Solid Mechanics extension, model the belt as an equivalent tensile member and compare its tight-side average normal stress with the assigned allowable stress.
